title: thread/started records a Codex thread id without a runtime check: a late notification can bind a default-home thread to a session switched to the read-only sandbox
outcome: Low from the round-3 Claude review of the read-only Codex sandbox change (delegation-775f3965-37a6-4698-a6b8-e41bd8f6ae67), plausible but not confirmed. src/codex_events.rs (about line 632) handles thread/started by calling set_external_session_id with no runtime-token check. The profile model assumes a thread is created only on the runtime whose profile was recorded when the session attached. The settings guard refuses a profile-crossing sandbox change only while a turn runs. The race: Stop while thread/start is in flight; the session goes idle; the user switches it to read-only (allowed, with runtime_reset_required set); a late thread/started from the old default app-server then records the thread. On Windows the session then holds a default-home thread with the read-only sandbox, the combination the guard refuses, and its next turn fails every command (writes are still refused, so enforcement holds). Whether a detached session still receives that notification depends on shared-session detach timing. Fix direction: record thread/started through set_external_session_id_if_runtime_matches with the runtime token, or check that the sandbox fits the profile when a thread id is recorded.
acceptance: A test delivers thread/started from a runtime the session is no longer attached to (after a profile-crossing sandbox switch) and shows the thread id is not recorded, or that the sandbox-to-profile fit is restored; the ordinary path still records the thread.
